_comment_order: Selection order (fleet-ops#3125, amended by fleet-ops#3323): PRODUCT work (PI_PICK_ROLE=product, exported by pi-issue-run and pi-packet-run) orders every candidate seat by VALUE from the rolling last-20-sessions ledger (~/.local/state/pi-packet/seat-yield.json, written each tick by libexec/fleet-metrics-export.py from pi-issue session files: yield AND mean usage.cost per session). value = yield / max(cost_per_session, 0.001). For packet_difficulty light the key is value alone — free seats carry cost ~0 (floored to 0.001) so they sort first at equal yield. For heavy/keystone the key is yield first (quality) then value — a free seat with 2% yield still loses to a paid seat with 70% yield on heavy work. A seat with fewer than 20 measured sessions gets provisional yield 0.5. Scout/canary/audit picks (any other PI_PICK_ROLE) stay free-first: free lanes (free_providers_in_order), then prepaid-quota (prepaid_providers_in_order, round-robin), then metered. cursor keystone/senior-review only at ~$16/day — #1133/#1167. _comment_ram_governor: 1.0 = the FALLBACK charge for repos without a worker_memory row (fleet-ops#4164, 2026-09-07). Admission no longer charges a flat 0.5 per worker: each active worker is charged its repo's MemoryHigh (0509 2.5G, fleet-ops 2.5G, heavy 1.0G from #3495) divided by this fallback, so a 0509 browser worker charges 2.5 units and a fleet-ops worker charges 2.5 units instead of the flat 1 (fleet-ops#3679, fleet-ops raised to 2.5G in #3885). Prior values: 0.6 measured 2026-08-27 (fleet-ops#1168: 10 live workers, subtrees ~470MB total, 11.5GB MemAvailable under load, p95 per-worker <0.5GB); 0.5 re-measured 2026-08-28 (fleet-ops#1558: n=4 workers, fleet-ops light MemoryPeak 0.11-0.63G, 0509 browser E2E MemoryPeak 2.06-2.39G); 2.0 raised 2026-09-05 (#3679 brake, stopped the MemoryHigh throttle storm). 2026-09-07 re-measurement (fleet-ops#4164): per-worker anon ~140MB steady, 24h systemd-oomd kills = 12 total (5 pi-issue@fleet-ops, 4 pi-issue@0509, 3 app-pi-issue.slice), every unit kill at the per-unit MemoryMax=4G cap while host MemAvailable stayed ~12GB of 16GB. The 2.0 charge was admitting 4 workers (at capacity total_cap=4) while the box had 12GB free — the admission governor measured free RAM, but the kills come from per-unit caps, which concurrency does not change. Lowering the fallback to 1.0 keeps the same per-worker charge (fleet-ops/0509 have no MemoryHigh row after #3930, so they fall back to this value) and lets the governor admit ~9-10 workers at 12GB free instead of 4, matching the realistic ceiling. Do NOT drop to 0.5 (the pre-#3679 value starved admission) or re-raise to 2.0 (the #3679 brake that over-charged after #3930 dropped the MemoryHigh band). Hard backstops remain (user-1000.slice MemoryHigh=12G, oomd 80%). Admission keeps cgroup memory.current. Historical class pin (fleet-ops#202): memory.current p95 was 822.6 MB vs process VmRSS ~35 MB — admission keeps cgroup memory.current, never RSS. CEILING NOTE (fleet-ops#3679): target_concurrent 25 is NOT reachable on 15 GB at 1.0-1.5 GiB per worker; the realistic ceiling is ~8-10 concurrent. Do NOT raise the slice MemoryHigh above 12G. Re-measure with bin/ram-metric-compare (heartbeat section 14). History: ~/.local/state/ram-measurement/ram-metric-compare.json. Changing ram_gb_per_worker also requires updating the scenario-4 assertion (and ok line) in tests/ram-metric-compare.test.sh in the same PR (fleet-ops#1190 — the #1168 drift where the config moved 1.5->0.6 but the test still locked 1.5). 2026-09-10 fleet-ops#4896 (Fable, Nish: low worker count until the re-measure is unacceptable): interim 1.5 GB — the 2.0 GB p50 was measured with workers running vitest --coverage forks (~0.8 GB each) + tsc -b (~2 GB) locally; fleet-ops#4893 (merged 2026-09-10 08:30Z) forbids both in-worker and 0509#2534 makes npm test coverage-free, so the old p50 no longer describes new workers. _comment_worker_memory: fleet-ops#1558 Q1=A: per-repo MemoryMax/MemoryHigh written by intake as a per-instance drop-in (pi-issue@<repo>-<N>.service.d/memory.conf) before systemctl start. Template pi-issue@.service keeps MemoryMax=6G/MemoryHigh=3G as the no-table fallback. fleet-ops#3679 raised MemoryHigh above measured p95 so workers stop living at the clamp (live measurement 2026-09-05: 0509 p95 2.07 GiB n=45, fleet-ops p95 1.02 GiB n=10; old MemoryHigh 0509 1536M and fleet-ops 1G had throttled=1). fleet-ops#3930 (2026-09-06) REMOVED the MemoryHigh throttle band entirely for fleet-ops + 0509 and raised MemoryMax to 4G: MemoryHigh is what makes oomd turn throttling into a kill of a random sibling (6 pi-issue@* kills in 1h on a 15 GB box; pi-issue@0509-1752 killed at a 94.3M peak — victim was not the offender). Keeping MemoryMax bounds every worker with a clean OOM at the cap; removing the throttle band means a worker that exceeds 4G is OOM-killed locally instead of oomd pressure-killing a sibling. Per-slice ManagedOOMMemoryPressureDurationSec is NOT a valid key in systemd 255 (verified systemd-analyze verify) — the 60s pressure window is already global via DefaultMemoryPressureDurationSec=60s in /etc/systemd/oomd.conf.d/99-fleet.conf. heavy class (fleet-ops#3281, part 8/9 of the manager-loop split): MemoryMax=3G/MemoryHigh=2G, written by intake for packet_difficulty heavy|keystone (a manager worker runs 8 parallel scouts + 1 implementer; measured flat worker peaks ~1.0 GB, so the RAM governor charges heavy workers at 1.0 GB). _comment_4643_cache_ttl: fleet-ops#4643: prompt prefix-cache only pays when the prefix is byte-identical AND lands inside the provider's cache-TTL window. The layout change (stable prefix first, volatile tail last) makes the prefix byte-identical across same-type packets; the TTL window decides whether the second packet still sees the cache. Per-provider windows (the metric fleet_prompt_cache_hit_ratio{provider,packet_type} is the PROOF — a lane that benefits shows a high ratio; a lane whose packets miss the window shows low): DeepSeek-family models (the DeepSeek flash family / deepseek-v4-pro) carry a SHORT ~5 min cache window (per the issue, 'DeepSeek-style ~5 min windows'); this covers the bulk of metered+prepaid lanes — crof, paretoinference, runinfra, entrim, straitly, ollama, bai, cline(deepseek), commandcode(deepseek), zenmux, openrouter(deepseek), mergegateway(deepseek), xkiro(deepseek), alibaba-coding(deepseek). For these, intake stagger (spawn_stagger_s) and the scout cadence must keep same-type packets inside the 5 min window or the prefix cache expires between them. GLM-family models (devin glm-5-2, z-ai/glm-5.3 on paretoinference/openrouter) and Anthropic Claude (mergegateway claude-sonnet-5, opencode-anthropic) and xAI Grok (xai-oauth grok-4.6) — exact TTLs are provider-doc-defined and NOT asserted here; treat them as inferred until the metric proves the lane benefits. No new scheduler: the existing spawn_stagger_s + scout timer cadence already space same-type packets; the metric is what tells us a lane is or is not inside its window. A lane below 85% for 6h fires FleetPromptCacheHitLow (config/fleet_rules.yml) -> am-executor, not Nish.

_comment_error_classes: fleet-ops#859: data-driven lane-fault registry. pi-issue-run iterates this map by trigger_order, calling _matcher_dispatch <matcher> <out> <err> once per class; the FIRST match fires its writer and stops (one writer wins, no double-bench). This replaces the former hard-coded quota-cap and 503-overload dispatch blocks, so a future lane-fault class is a config-only addition (a row in seat-caps.json + a matcher function + a case branch in _matcher_dispatch / _writer_dispatch), not a third copy of the three-file pattern. The writers keep their own provider-default resolution (quota_bench_default_s / 503_bench_default_s in the provider rows below); this map is dispatch wiring only, not the default-window value. spawn_fail and mid_session_death are NOT here: they have time-based guards (spawn_elapsed < SPAWN_FAIL_MAX_S / > SPAWN_FAIL_MAX_S) that the generic matcher contract cannot express, so they stay as explicit blocks in pi-issue-run.
